newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-DAVENPORT EDGES WILLIAMS AT EVERT CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAVENPORT EDGES WILLIAMS AT EVERT CUP.

text.p: It took a monumental effort but fourth seed Lindsay Davenport edged 16-year-old qualifier Venus Williams for a 6-4 5-7 7-6 (7-1) quarter-final victory Wednesday at the Evert Cup.
The eighth-ranked Davenport reached the semifinals here for a second consecutive year, but the 211th-ranked Williams stole the limelight.
In only her 10th tournament since becoming a professional in 1994 -- and her first of the year -- Williams displayed why she is expected to be a force on the WTA Tour.
"Definitely she's going to be one of the best players in the coming years, if not real soon," Davenport said.
"Everybody knew she was playing excellent tennis. I knew it was going to be a tough match. You know she's going to go for broke."

One of the women's semifinals features top-seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain against sixth-seed Irina Spirlea of Romania. The fourth-ranked Sanchez Vicario moved into the semis Tuesday and the 11th-ranked Spirlea recorded a 6-4 6-2 quarter-final win over 13th-seed Nathalie Tauziat Wednesday.
The other semifinal pits Davenport against ninth-seed Mary Joe Fernandez of the United States. The 14th-ranked Fernandez upset second seed Conchita Martinez of Spain 6-4 6-4.
The match between Davenport and Williams was a slugfest under the lights. Both players are tall, powerful and aggressive.
"I went out there and played the best I could, and I played hard," said Williams, who upset ninth seed Iva Majoli in the third round. "I had a good match. I was really challenged. That's fun."

The match saw 20 service breaks -- five in the first set, nine in the second set, six in the third set -- as each player pressured the other into attempting a great first serve or face the consequences on the second serve.
Davenport, who won the Oklahoma City tournament two weeks ago, served for the match in both the second and third sets at 5-4. But the cocky Williams was not willing to be brushed aside.
In the second set, Williams won the final two games to force a final set.
The third set went down to the wire where Davenport, 20, showed what a little experience can do. She won all but one point in the tiebreaker.
